Weekly Sales — How to use this tab
The agenda for the Wednesday sales meeting. For each account owner (Primary in Clients › Account Management), pick only the partners worth discussing this week and write a short update.
+ Add partner — your own clients and deals first; search for anyone else's Situation · Remark · Meeting notes / decision + Add note — anything not tied to one partner Drag ⋮⋮ beside the number to put the most important first Numbers fill in from CRM data
※ Anyone can edit, in Korean or English. Each field saves when you leave it. Click a client to open it in Clients, a deal to open it in Pipeline. Last week's meeting note for the same partner shows above it.

Clients — How to use this tab
Browse the full client list and revenue summary. Click a client on the left to see their details on the right.
Sort By — revenue / order count / most recent order / alphabetical Period — set a date range to compare revenue across periods Groups — bundle clients into named groups for easy management ⚠ Inactive — log comments for clients with no recent orders Reorders — every client's expected next order + products whose reorder cycle is getting longer (churn signal) 🌱 — brand has ordered 10+ SKUs (a growth-potential signal; hidden once already Tier 1)
※ Click a client → view order history, unit price changes, and inactive notes. Remarks are saved in your browser.

Delays — How to use this tab
Record where and why late orders lost time, stage by stage, and set the stage lead-time standards from it. Planning confirms each verdict.
Review — per late line: stage, cause code, could we have prevented it; Planning confirms Cases — lines the departments review together, questions to copy, answers Open orders — lines that miss the required date at standard pace, stage targets Lead times · Sources — the standards, Kanban and Cin7 connection status

Pipeline — How to use this tab
Manage new development deals on a Kanban board. Drag and drop cards to move them through stages.
Contacted → Lead → Quoted → Negotiating → Won / Drop
Reading deal cards
⚠ 1M Stalled ≥30 days — click to add a note. Highlight clears once a note is saved 🔴🟡🟢 Badge colour can only be changed by managers — set in ⚙ Manager Settings D+N Expected close date overdue ♻ Revived Revived from Drop
searchDeal Search — type a keyword to search across title, customer, owner, notes, and activity log simultaneously. Fuzzy matching included. Click a result to open the deal directly.
Stall Filter — use 1M+ / 2M+ / 3M+ buttons to show only deals stalled beyond that period (based on Quote Sent date).
Activity Log — log emails, calls, and meetings via the Activity Log button on each card. Stage changes are logged automatically and cannot be edited.
restart_altRevival — drag a Drop deal back to an active stage to revive it. Enter a revival reason; full history is preserved. Owner Scorecard
🎯 Sharpshooter Most Won deals 💰 Top Earner Highest Won value 🌱 Most Active Most total deals
Filter by period (All / 3M / 6M / 1Y) based on Close Date. Win rate = Won ÷ total deals; green if ≥25%.
※ Moving to Won/Drop prompts for a close reason. A confirmation popup appears before closing an unsaved deal.

Production — How to use this tab
One oERP export (Sales_statistics.xlsx) is the mother data for both the Planning / Production team and Sales. Upload the newest file in Data each week and every view updates — no deploy needed.
Production — line gap warnings, new orders vs monthly target, production status, readiness and client hold Sales — what to win to keep each line busy, client holds to chase, backlog and forecast Output history — the previous production output view Data — upload, changes since last file, data checks, capacity and targets
※ Client hold = waiting on the client (artwork, client-supplied material, formula sign-off, deposit). Those orders are left out of backlog days, gap warnings and factory delivery risk, and are listed by owner in Sales.

Credit — How to use this tab
Automatically calculates the expected Deposit / Balance invoice amounts for every SO of a client, so you don't have to hunt through Xero one order at a time.
Deposit = order value × Deposit % × (1 + GST) Balance = finished qty × unit price × (1 + GST) − Deposit 📥 CSV — paste straight into the Excel sheet
※ Expected amounts only -- actual invoiced/paid status isn't linked to Xero yet. Deposit % comes from the Clients tab, GST from the Customer Profile Tax Rate (blank = 15% for NZD, 0% otherwise).

Forecast — How to use this tab
Projects future revenue across three views.
📦 Existing Clients — repeat order forecast based on current clients 🎯 Pipeline — deal est. value × probability (weighted) 📈 Combined — total outlook combining both sources
※ Pipeline forecast improves as you add and update deals in the Pipeline tab.

Outreach — How to use this tab
Prospecting for new OEM clients (Project WhaleHunting): our strategy and top picks, research on the 12 target companies, and a generator for each one's email sequence, call script and attachments. The first touch is always email, to a published address only.
Strategy — positioning, proof points, who to contact, top picks, email sequence, call method, open decisions Research & approach — findings, email route, contacts and angle per company Draft generator — pick a preset to write the four emails and the call script Market screening — filter every brand in the market by our criteria
※ The yellow "Internal notes" box is internal only — never paste it into outreach. Emails 2–4 go as replies in the first email's thread. Copy To / Subject / body separately or use "Open in Gmail", then attach the files in Gmail. Your signature is saved in this browser.

View OEM bulk orders by year. Select a year using the buttons at the top. Use this to track actual performance against annual order targets and monitor production schedules by product.

Update Log — How to use this tab
Every CRM change is logged here with a version number. Big redesigns bump the first number (1.0 → 2.0), feature-level updates bump the middle number (1.0 → 1.1 → 1.2), and small fixes or refinements of a recent update bump the last number (1.0 → 1.0.1).
